diseases.description: A fast virus that spreads to tank mates.
Bacteria from spoiled food and dirty water eat away at the fins.
A parasite that slowly hops between fish.
Overeating trouble. Rarely deadly and usually passes on its own.

food.name: Flakes
food.blurb: Cheap everyday food. Now and then a spoiled flake makes a fish sick.

food.name: Algae wafers
food.blurb: Sinking wafers of algae and greens, for grazers and bottom feeders.

food.name: Premium pellets
food.blurb: Filling and much less likely to cause illness.

food.name: Frozen brine shrimp
food.blurb: Tiny shrimp that drift slowly down. Small fish go mad for them.

food.name: Frozen bloodworms
food.blurb: Rich midge larvae, a treat for most fish. Frozen food carries a little more risk.

eggTiers.name: Rare eggs
eggTiers.blurb: A mix of everyday and rare fish. Rare ones are much likelier than in simple eggs.

eggTiers.name: Wild tetra eggs
eggTiers.blurb: Caught in South American and African rivers: tetras you can't get anywhere else, some of them very rare.

eggTiers.name: Ultra rare eggs
eggTiers.blurb: Rare fish, with a chance of something exotic.

backgrounds.name: Sandy shallows
backgrounds.blurb: Pale sand, dark rocks and a little seaweed in bright, shallow water.

backgrounds.name: Open ocean
backgrounds.blurb: Deep blue water with sunbeams from far above.

backgrounds.name: Planted stream
backgrounds.blurb: Lush green and red stem plants over smooth river stones.

backgrounds.name: Driftwood forest
backgrounds.blurb: Tangled roots and fallen leaves in tea-coloured blackwater, like a tetra's home river.

backgrounds.name: Coral reef
backgrounds.blurb: A sunlit reef bursting with colourful corals.

backgrounds.name: Shipwreck
backgrounds.blurb: An old wooden wreck on the sea floor, overgrown with coral.

backgrounds.name: Reef arch
backgrounds.blurb: A great rock arch over white sand, kelp and a shoal of fish under sunbeams.

backgrounds.name: Bass pond
backgrounds.blurb: Bass cruising between reeds and a sunken log under a ceiling of lily pads.

backgrounds.name: Lily pad shallows
backgrounds.blurb: Green light through lily pads over a mossy lake bed lined with reeds.

filters.name: Hang-on-back filter
filters.blurb: Cleaner water, and it lasts longer.

filters.name: Plant-room sump
filters.blurb: A big sump in the room behind the wall, pumping the whole wall aquarium through its filter media.

filters.name: Drum filter and UV system
filters.blurb: Public aquarium filtration: a self-cleaning drum filter with a UV steriliser.

heaters.name: Basic heater
heaters.blurb: The water drifts a little either side of the setting.

heaters.name: Twin inline heaters
heaters.blurb: Two heaters on the sump's return line, for a tank too big for any one heater.

heaters.name: Heat exchanger with controller
heaters.blurb: A titanium heat exchanger run by a controller: holds the exact temperature in all that water.

bubblers.name: Air stone
bubblers.blurb: Enough air for a small group.

bubblers.name: Silent air pump
bubblers.blurb: Air for a crowded tank, rarely breaks.

bubblers.name: Air blower and manifold
bubblers.blurb: A blower feeding air lines all along the wall aquarium.

bubblers.name: Oxygen injection system
bubblers.blurb: Pure oxygen dissolved into the return line: air for every fish the wall aquarium can hold.

projects.name: Health check-ups
projects.teaches: The arrows by a fish's health and comfort open up to show why they're rising or falling, and by how much.

projects.name: Temperature preferences
projects.teaches: Learn the temperature range every fish you've discovered likes. The heater offers the best setting for a tank.

projects.name: Tank mate behaviour
projects.teaches: Health notes say exactly who a fish is afraid of, fights with or likes, and the journal lists how every kind you've discovered gets on.

projects.name: Water testing kit
projects.teaches: Measure the pH of every tank: how acidic (below 7) or alkaline (above 7) the water is.

projects.name: Feeding study
projects.teaches: A fish shows it loves a food the first time it eats one of its favourites, and favourites you've seen already are written up.

projects.name: Breeding biology
projects.teaches: The breeding tab explains why each fish isn't ready to breed, and you learn which kinds lay eggs and which give birth.

projects.name: Shoaling behaviour
projects.teaches: Learn how many of its own kind each fish wants around it.

projects.name: Fish pathology
projects.teaches: Sick fish show how far along their illness is and which medicine cures it.

projects.name: Plant preferences
projects.teaches: Learn which fish love plants in their tank.

projects.name: pH preferences
projects.teaches: Learn the pH range every fish you've discovered likes.

projects.name: Ageing study
projects.teaches: Learn how long each kind of fish lives before it starts to slow down.

boothUpgrades.name: Price board
boothUpgrades.blurb: A chalk board of what other aquariums charge, so you can see where your price sits.

boothUpgrades.name: Visitor counter
boothUpgrades.blurb: A turnstile that counts everyone coming and going, and how many walked off at the booth.

boothUpgrades.name: Computerised ticketing
boothUpgrades.blurb: A ticketing system that knows exactly what visitors will pay. The estimate is spot on.

gear.name: His own wetsuit and tank
gear.blurb: No more rented gear: he can stay down longer and look further.

gear.name: Dive computer and torch
gear.blurb: Deeper dives, and a light for the caves where shy fish hide.

gear.name: Underwater scooter
gear.blurb: He covers a whole reef in one dive.

gear.name: Rebreather
gear.blurb: No bubbles to scare the fish: the rarest come right up to him.
